methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $12M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 5 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

private.name: Humanoid
private.rationale: Same sector (Robotics & Manufacturing), same stage (Series A), post-money $1.35B

data.narrative:
Laminar is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Annie Lu and David Lu that has raised $12.4M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of five private peers in robotics and manufacturing at Series A and adjacent stages, supplemented by one public comparable (ticker 277810.KQ).

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method uses total capital raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage progression, yielding $25M. The peer-median method benchmarks against five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Generalist AI ($2.0B Series B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B Series B), Humanoid ($1.4B Series A), and Walden Robotics ($1.1B Seed)—producing a median valuation of $1.6B and range of $1.1B to $2.0B.

The wide dispersion between methods reflects fundamental uncertainty regarding Laminar's position within its peer cohort. The triangulated range spans $21M to $1.9B with a median of $837M. The stage-progression floor assumes minimal market differentiation relative to capital deployed, while the peer-median reflects recent market valuations in robotics that may not yet incorporate company-specific traction or risk factors. Critical uncertainties include revenue, capital efficiency relative to peers, technological differentiation, and whether the peer set—dominated by Series B+ rounds—appropriately anchors a Series A company. Resolution of these factors will be essential to narrowing this range.
